S.summaryInstructions:
You and Mr Example separated in September 2026 after 12 years of marriage. You have two children, aged 9 and 6, who live with you.
You want to divorce, agree arrangements for the children and resolve your finances, including the future of the family home.
S.specificAdvice: You asked whether you can stay in the family home with the children. The children's housing needs will be an important factor, but the home is also a major asset and no outcome can be guaranteed. I recommend that you do not agree to sell or transfer the property until full financial disclosure has been exchanged.
S.nextSteps:
Complete and return the enclosed financial information questionnaire
Attend a Mediation Information and Assessment Meeting (MIAM)
I will prepare the divorce application for your approval
S.docsNeeded:
Marriage certificate
Bank statements for the last 12 months
Mortgage statement and a recent property valuation
Pension statements
Your last three payslips
S.costStage: the divorce application and financial disclosure
S.venue:
Central Family Court
First Avenue House
42-49 High Holborn
London WC1V 6NP
S.docsToBring:
Photographic ID
Your copy of the Form E and supporting documents
Any new documents received from the other side
S.outcomeSummary: The judge reviewed the financial disclosure exchanged so far and identified the main issues as the future of the family home and the division of pensions. The judge was not satisfied that the pension information was complete.
S.orders:
Both parties must file updated pension valuations
The case is listed for a Financial Dispute Resolution appointment (FDR)
S.directions:
By 4pm on 20 November 2026: exchange pension valuations
By 4pm on 4 December 2026: file and serve answers to the questionnaires
S.orderStatus: A sealed copy of the order is enclosed
S.clientActions:
Ask each pension provider for a Cash Equivalent Transfer Value
Send me your answers to the questionnaire by 27 November 2026
S.purpose: Update following receipt of the other side's Form E
S.discussion:
Spoke to the client about the other side's Form E. The client was concerned that two bank accounts listed in the Form E were not in the earlier voluntary disclosure.
The client confirmed she has no knowledge of the source of the new funds.
S.instructionsRec: Client instructs me to raise the undisclosed accounts by letter to the other side's solicitors and to ask for six months of statements.
S.adviceGiven: Advised that full and frank disclosure is required and that we can ask questions under the court timetable. Advised that raising the point early may avoid a dispute at the First Appointment.
S.docsNote:
Form E of Mr Example (received today)
Bank statements (client's, received last week)
S.actions:
Draft letter raising the accounts | Case worker | Within 2 working days
Send draft to client for approval | Case worker | Same day
Send client's payslips | Client | By Friday
S.enclosures:
Sealed copy of the final order
Sealed copy of the consent order
S.c_tasks:
Send a copy of the consent order to your mortgage lender and to each pension provider
Update your records at HM Land Registry if the property has been transferred to you
S.careServices:
Advise you on the divorce, the arrangements for your children and your finances
Prepare and issue the divorce application
Obtain and exchange financial disclosure
Negotiate a settlement and, if agreed, prepare a consent order for the court
Represent you at court hearings, including instructing counsel where appropriate
S.pr_status: Both financial statements have now been exchanged. The main issues are the family home and the pension.
S.pr_done:
Received Mr Example's Form E and supporting documents
Wrote to his solicitors about the two accounts that were not disclosed
Asked each pension provider for a Cash Equivalent Transfer Value
S.pr_waiting:
Cash Equivalent Transfer Values | the pension providers
Reply about the undisclosed accounts | Mr Example's solicitors
S.pr_next: Once we have the pension valuations I will advise you on the options for the family home and for dividing the pensions.
S.pr_actions:
Send me your answers to the questionnaire
Tell me if the children's arrangements change
S.apt_purpose: To go through the pension valuations and your options
S.dr_docs:
Bank statements for the last 12 months
Your last three payslips
A recent mortgage statement
S.dr_reason: The court expects full financial disclosure, and we must send your documents to the other side by the deadline in the order.
S.dr_how: Please email clear scans or photographs, or post copies to us
S.cu_narr: Most of the work this month was reviewing Mr Example's disclosure and preparing questions.
S.of_terms:
You keep the family home and take on the mortgage
Mr Example keeps his pension
There is a lump sum of GBP 25,000 to you
Each side pays their own costs
S.of_basis: Without prejudice save as to costs
S.of_advice: The offer deals with the home but leaves out the pensions, which are a significant asset. I need the pension valuations before I can say whether the offer is fair.
S.of_pros:
You would keep the home for the children
It would end the case sooner and cut costs
S.of_cons:
The pensions are not shared
The lump sum may be low once the pensions are valued
S.of_counter: I suggest we ask for the pensions to be valued and shared before any agreement.
S.ts_subject: Jane Example and John Example: financial remedy
S.ts_body: Mr Example's Form E lists two bank accounts that were not in his earlier voluntary disclosure.
S.ts_requests:
Explain why the accounts were not disclosed earlier
Provide statements for both accounts for the last 12 months
S.tc_addr:
Central Family Court
First Avenue House
42-49 High Holborn
London WC1V 6NP
S.tc_body: We enclose the parties' updated pension valuations, as the order of 12 October 2026 required.
S.ct_summary: The parties were married for 12 years and have two children. The main assets are the family home and two pensions.
S.ct_tasks:
Hold a conference with our client before the hearing
Advise on the pension sharing options
Represent our client at the hearing
S.ct_bundle:
Form E of each party
The order of 12 October 2026
Our chronology
S.ct_fee: The brief fee has been agreed with your clerk.
S.cs_docs:
Draft consent order
Statement of information form for the consent order (check the court's current form and number)
Court fee
S.cs_agreed: The parties have agreed that the family home is transferred to Ms Example, and that the pensions are shared in equal parts.
S.abuseSummary:
On 3 September 2026 he pushed you against a wall and threatened to kill you.
He has sent you repeated abusive messages, and on 14 September 2026 he waited outside your workplace.
S.urgency: You told us you are afraid to go home and that the other party has said he will find you.
S.laScope: Application for a non-molestation order and an occupation order, including a without notice application
S.laContribution: No contribution is payable under your certificate
S.daEvidence:
Police report (crime reference CRN 01/2345/26)
Letter from your GP
S.evidenceNeeded:
Screenshots of the messages
Photographs of your injuries
S.c_represent:
On 2 October 2026 the court held a without notice hearing at the Central Family Court. I represented you.
On 16 October 2026 the court held the return date hearing. Counsel instructed by us represented you.
S.c_meaning:
The non-molestation order stops the other party from using or threatening violence against you, and from intimidating, harassing or pestering you. Breaking it is a criminal offence. If it is broken, call the police and tell me.
The order applies for 12 months.
S.laChargeOutcome: The statutory charge does not apply in your case.

audit.a: Reminder added: Chase police for the log
